chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Salama ibn Muhraz, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'An Armenian man died and bequeathed to me.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'And what is an Armenian?' I said, 'A Nabatean from the Nabateans of the mountains, died and bequeathed to me his legacy, and left a daughter.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Give her half.'

He (the narrator) said, 'So I informed Zurara of that, and he said to me, 'I was being cautious for you; rather, the wealth is for her.' So I entered upon him (peace be upon him) afterwards and said, 'May Allah improve you! Our companions claimed that you were cautious with me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, by Allah, I was not cautious with you, but I was cautious over you lest you be held responsible (for giving too little). So did anyone know of that?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So give her what remains.'

key_terms.أَرْمَانِيّاً: Armenian (a specific ethnic group mentioned in the context of non-Arab Muslims)
key_terms.نَبَطِيٌّ: Nabatean (a people from the mountains, used here to clarify the ethnicity)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a daughter who is the sole heir?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'taqiyya' (precautionary dissimulation) in inheritance rulings, where the Imam initially advised giving half to the daughter to protect the executor from potential liability regarding unknown heirs. Upon clarification that no other claimants existed, the Imam corrected the ruling to the full estate, highlighting the distinction between precautionary measures and definitive legal entitlements. This incident underscores the dynamic nature of fiqh where practical wisdom and risk management inform the application of Quranic shares.
